title: Maximum Linear Stock Score
statement:
`prices[i]` is a stock's price on day `i`. Choose a non-empty set of days (a single day is allowed). The choice is **linear** when every two consecutive chosen days `a < b` satisfy `prices[b] - prices[a] == b - a`: the price climbs by exactly the number of days between them.

The score of a choice is the sum of the prices on its chosen days. Return the largest score any linear choice can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

The rule `prices[b] - prices[a] == b - a` can be rearranged to `prices[b] - b == prices[a] - a`. So two days may sit next to each other in a linear choice exactly when they share the same value of `prices[i] - i`, and since that value is shared, every day with the same key is compatible with every other one. A best choice therefore takes **all** days of one key (prices are positive, so adding a day only helps). Trying every pair of days with a DP works but costs O(n²); grouping by the key in a hash map costs O(n).

## Approach

1. Keep a map `totals` from each key `prices[i] - i` to the sum of prices seen with that key.
2. For each day `i`, compute `key`, add `prices[i]` to its running `total`, and store it back.
3. Track the largest running total in `best` and return it at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`prices = [1, 5, 3, 7, 8]` gives keys `1-0 = 1`, `5-1 = 4`, `3-2 = 1`, `7-3 = 4`, `8-4 = 4`. Key 1 collects `1 + 3 = 4`; key 4 collects `5 + 7 + 8 = 20`. The largest total is `20`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant-time map updates.
- Space: O(n) for the map in the worst case (all keys different).

## Pitfalls

- The key must subtract the index; grouping by equal prices or by equal differences between neighbours is wrong.
- Chosen days do not have to be adjacent, so do not stop a group when a different key appears in between.
- Totals reach about 10^14, beyond 32-bit integers; use a 64-bit type (`long`) in Java and C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `totals` | map from key to the sum of prices with that key so far |
| `best` | the largest group total seen so far |
| `i` | the current day |
| `key` | `prices[i] - i`, the value shared by compatible days |
| `total` | the updated sum for the current key |

narration.2: Map each key prices[i] - i to the total of the prices that share it.
narration.3: No day has been chosen yet, so the best score starts at 0.
narration.4: Visit every day once, left to right.
narration.5: Days with the same price-minus-index can all be chained together.
narration.6: Add today's price to the running total of its group.
narration.8: Keep the largest group total seen so far.
narration.10: The best linear choice takes every day of the heaviest group.
